prompt:
Create a 3x1 sprite sheet for a modern 16-bit-style pixel-art RPG: one MONSTER in three battle poses.

Image 1 is a LAYOUT GUIDE: three cells on white. In each cell the light-grey box shows where the monster stands and how big it is, the grey line is the ground, and the arrow shows the facing: the monster faces RIGHT, toward the heroes. Draw the SAME monster once in every cell, filling its box. Never draw the grey box, line or arrow.

Image 2 is the HOUSE STYLE: an approved hero sprite sheet from this same game. Match its sprite-pixel size, black outlines, flat shading with 2-3 tones per colour and level of detail exactly, but do NOT copy the hero; it is a different character.

Image 3 is an APPROVED MONSTER sheet from this same game (a DIFFERENT monster, idle | attack | hurt): match its sprite-pixel size, rendering, shading, outline weight and level of detail, and how much the poses move. Do NOT copy that monster's body, colours or equipment.

Render as true pixel art: the monster about 56-72 pixels tall in sprite pixels, every sprite pixel a hard-edged square, no anti-aliasing, no gradients.

Monster: a tall gaunt elder vampire with long straight white hair, a pale grey face with sunken red eyes and small fangs, a tall stiff black collar rising behind the head like a crown with sharp points, a long black coat with dark red trim, a black cape shaped like bat wings joined from the shoulders along both arms to the wrists, long clawed fingers; centred in its own cell with empty space on both sides, the collar points well below the top of the grey box. Keep every detail identical in every cell. FACE: his gaunt pale face with red eyes under long white hair is readable.

Cells:
- left cell: idle, a ready battle stance facing right.
- middle cell: attack, leaning forward toward the heroes, one clawed hand reaching out with the elbow bent and its bat-wing cape spread under that arm, the other arm and its half of the cape kept close to the body (not flung out behind), the hand and the whole cape well inside the middle cell, facing right.
- right cell: hurt, knocked back, the white hair flying, both arms raised in front of the face with the bat-wing cape folded across the body, recoiling away from the heroes (leaning left), still facing right.

MOVEMENT: the attack and hurt cells are dramatic ACTION frames, not static stances. Use a clear diagonal line of action through the whole body, shift the weight onto one leg and lean the torso toward the heroes, the elbows bent, so every reaching part stays well inside its own cell. The bat-wing cape is joined to the arms and moves with them, kept within the cell. Draw only the parts named in the description: no second cape, and no smear or motion lines. Each of the three silhouettes must be clearly different. BODY: in every cell, standing on two feet, both feet on the ground line. No mist, smoke or ground effects.

One monster per cell and nothing else: no props on the ground, no effects outside the monster, no text.
Background: solid flat magenta (#FF00FF) everywhere, no floor, no shadows, no borders.
Avoid: two creatures in one cell, different creatures in different cells, background scenery, floor tiles, shadows on the ground, magic effects outside the cell, text, frame, border, grid lines, blurry, soft shading, gradient, 3d render, slicked black hair, a red vest, a separate cape, a crown on the head, a weapon, real bat wings on the back, a young face.
